The single path every upstream call takes when it is not routed through a specific pool below.
Off, so upstream calls go out directly
A self-registered upstream endpoint beyond the built-in provider catalog. A connection references it by id.
No node is registered. Add one to route through a custom endpoint.
A named outbound path a connection or a provider strategy can be bound to instead of routing directly.
No pool exists. Add one to give a connection or a provider strategy somewhere to route through.
Binds one proxy pool to a provider id, for every connection under that provider that has no pool of its own.
A rotation strategy across several proxy pools for one provider. Only a single pool binding per provider exists in the settings schema, so this screen can bind or clear one pool and nothing more.
Registers a new upstream endpoint that a connection can be pointed at.
Updates the node's prefix, API dialect and base URL, and cascades them into every connection bound to it.
Removes this node, every provider connection registered against it, and every model alias that points at it, in one step.
None. A deleted node, its connections and its aliases cannot be restored.
Registers a new outbound path a connection or a provider strategy can be bound to.
Updates this pool. Changing its strictness updates every connection and every provider strategy currently bound to it, atomically.
No connection is bound to this pool. It is deleted immediately.
None. A deleted pool cannot be restored.
Every upstream call not routed through a specific pool uses this proxy from now on.
Every upstream call not routed through a specific pool goes out directly from now on.
Leave empty to keep the current URL
Strict: a connection or strategy bound here fails outright rather than falling back to a direct connection
